industry.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the United States consumer surveys fell again (University of Michigan 46.3 preliminary October, down 1.8; Conference Board 81.9 in September, down 6.7; Goldman Sachs 19 Oct), consumer discretionary lagged with technology and communication services in the week's rotation (Jefferies, 17 Oct), and the European consumer was again not read, so the row rests on the US reading and on the regime. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, D prior, the largest industry in the universe at 138 stocks. Counter-case: Retail physical reads B and Online retail A on relative strength, Hotels C, which is where cheap good businesses accumulate, and a double notch on 138 stocks shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists; the exceptions are carried at sector level (H.3 Neutral).

sector.why: Double Underweight, carried, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': the Budget funded Your First Home (£4.7bn of government-backed lending for about 70,000 first-time buyers) and the sector closed about 7% lower (Barratt Redrow minus 6.6%, Taylor Wimpey minus 7.3%, Persimmon minus 6.9%) because first loans come no earlier than April 2027 and miss the spring selling season, so the memo's one-notch test is withdrawn; five-year fixed mortgages near 6%, a Bank of England rise to 4.00% almost priced for 5-Nov-26 and 2027 growth cut to 1.0% decide the row. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, F prior. Counter-case: net-cash balance sheets, two kinds of winner (low-price volume builders, partnership builders) and homebuilders bottom before rates peak. Re-test when the scheme's caps are published and loans are paid.

geography.why: Neutral, carried as a judgement with the evidence now read both ways, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': the Budget removed a UK-specific fiscal tail risk from the discount rate without lowering it (headroom £15bn, both rules met, the 10-year gilt about 5.32% and its lowest in over a month, gilts outperforming Bunds and Treasuries by about 5 basis points), and the UK data beat on every count (growth 0.7% on three months, employment up 102,000, purchasing managers' indices beating; Pacific, 26 October); against it, 2027 growth cut to 1.0% from 1.6%, unemployment 5.1% in 2027, the energy price cap up about 16% in January, a Bank of England rise to 4.00% almost priced for 5-Nov-26, and banks made the first payer in the next shock. Neutral against Underweight was tested; the data say the consumer slows rather than breaks, so Neutral, with no weight carried in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). 22 of the 144 Pool stocks are UK-listed. Counter-case: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance on 5-Nov-26, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
